item.text: {"text":"NextItNet’s foundation is stacked dilated causal convolutions with residual connections, expanding receptive fields while preserving sequence order. The searches did not identify a directly matching 2024–2026 NextItNet paper demonstrating learned dilation plus time-aware intent gating. Related evidence supports selective context: GAT4Rec (2024) uses a GRU-derived gate to select informative subsequences; ConvRec (2026) progressively aggregates neighboring interactions through hierarchical convolution. These motivate adaptive context selection but do not establish gains for a gated NextItNet. Sources: [NextItNet](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.05163), [GAT4Rec](https://www.mdpi.com/2227-7390/12/14/2189/html), [ConvRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.04723).\n\nA compatible experimental hypothesis is to retain NextItNet’s causal residual backbone and add jointly trained gates over convolutional features at several fixed dilations. Condition gates on causal hidden states and observed timestamp gaps, allowing recent coherent interactions to dominate while retaining useful older context. This is an inference from related work, not a published or validated result. ScaleRec (2026) provides adjacent motivation through multi-scale preference modeling and adaptive suppression of redundant interactions, although its backbone is Transformer-based. Evaluate gated dilation first, then timestamp conditioning, using the fixed four-category macro validation HR@10 protocol. Keep one jointly trained model/checkpoint per category, final-nonpadding readout, and identical training/predictor architectures. Source: [ScaleRec](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0306457325002596)."}
